title: Duel Decks: Izzet vs. Golgari: card flavor text

paragraphs.text: It traps an explosion within its stony skin.
When asked how much power is required, Izzet mages always answer "more."
"Diametrically opposing energies in self-sealed plasmodermic bubbles make great pets!" —Trivaz, Izzet mage
"The blazekite is a simple concept, really—just a vehicular application of dragscoop ionics and electropropulsion magnetronics." —Juzba, Izzet tinker
Like many Izzet creations, weirds are based on wild contradictions yet somehow manage to work.
He's an oxymoron.
It chews open Mirrodin's husk and feeds on the outpouring of energy.
He ensures not only whether but also when and where the lightning strikes twice.
The mizzium-sphere array drove her mind deep into the thought field, where only the rarest motes of genius may be plucked.
"I don't *think* so."
"Jund is a wounded world. Beware its searing blood spilling out onto the surface." —Rakka Mar
The Izzet signet is redesigned often, each time becoming closer to a vanity portrait of Niv-Mizzet.
On Bant, a sigil is both a prize of honor and a bond of duty. The one who bears it may be called to fulfill that charge at any moment.
"But then . . . oh, but . . . which means . . . which would lead to . . . exactly!"
Leave the door to the past even slightly ajar and it could be blown off its hinges.
The clouds grew thick, and then they grew teeth.
"This abomination never belonged in our world. I'm merely setting it free." —Dierk, geistmage
The dwarves call their quicksilver techniques "improvisational weaponsmithing."
"My brain hurts."
Its host's final curse lies captured within.
To those in tune with the Firemind, there is no difference between knowledge and flame.
Niv-Mizzet's genius and vanity reverberate throughout the mirrored halls of Nivix.
"Look at her, once filled with innocence. Death has a way of wringing away such . . . deficiencies." —Savra
Cast out of the Conclave generations ago, these elves found a home in the corrupted districts of the Golgari.
Devouring books is only the beginning. The librarian's next.
"They may show up with the wrong thigh bone or mandible, but they always show up." —Zul Ashur, lich lord
The only thing it likes more than discovering a pit of bones is adding to it.
It reacted to Naya's overabundant food supply by growing additional mouths.
She remembers every word spoken, from the hero's oath to the baby's cry.
Man's best fungus.
The juiciest prey is that which grows lazy, thinking itself beyond the reach of danger.
"Victory in the pits is almost as rewarding as the methods I use to achieve it."
Like corpse-worms through a carapace, rotwurms slide through the hollowed bones of the undercity.
It eats and eats until the juiciest morsel it can find is itself.
Depending on your point of view, the seal represents a proud guardian of the natural cycle or one who has sold her soul to darkness for eternal life.
Mercadians not wealthy enough to buy a tomb are thrown into a bog called "the Ghoul's Larder."
The demon's yoke is part leash, part noose.
The Golgari don't bury their dead. They plant them.
"All matter, animate or not, rots when exposed to time. We merely speed up the process." —Ezoc, Golgari rot farmer
"The living cannot understand the benefits of death." —Chaeska, Keeper of Tresserhorn
After fear and weakness rot away, that which remains is stronger than its living form.
"Nothing in nature goes to waste, not even the rotting corpse of a good-for-nothing, blood-sucking vampire." —Halana of Ulvenwald
Twilight falls. We rise. —Necropolis inscription
